WORKSHEET · CLASS 34 · AGES 4–5

Animals and Seasons Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A animals-and-seasons worksheet for ages 4–5: match each animal to its season, circle the hibernating bear, sort the animal cards and trace the word ANIMAL. Print it for a quiet table session.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/animals-and-seasons/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Match

    Draw a line from each animal to the season where it belongs.

  2. 2

    Circle

    One animal sleeps all winter — find it and circle it.

  3. 3

    Sort

    Put each animal card into the right season group.

  4. 4

    Trace

    Trace the big dotted word ANIMAL, then write it yourself.

  5. 5

    Draw

    Draw one animal in its seasonal home in the last box.

Before you start, have the words ready: The four season names, and one familiar animal for each — a spring bird, a summer butterfly, an autumn squirrel, a winter bear.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

Seasons change what animals do — eating, sleeping, travelling and hiding all follow the weather.

Linking animals to seasons builds the idea that living things respond to the world, not just to us — early science thinking on paper.

  • Season vocabulary
  • Animal names and habitats
  • Sorting and matching
  • Early science reasoning
  • Word tracing
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: Every animal has a favourite kind of weather. Let us find out who likes which season.

Questions to ask: Where does the bear go in winter? Which of these animals have you seen for real — and in which season?

Parent tips: One sheet, one sitting. If the tracing stalls, do the matching first and come back to the word.

Home practice: On the next walk or park trip, spot one real animal and name its season together.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 34 · AGES 4–5

Autumn and Winter Sorting Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A autumn-and-winter sorting worksheet for ages 4–5: match seasons to pictures, circle the cold-day clothes, sort the two seasons and trace AUTUMN. Printable.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/autumn-and-winter-sorting/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Match

    Match each season picture to its name.

  2. 2

    Circle

    Circle every piece of clothing a cold day asks for.

  3. 3

    Sort

    Cut and paste each picture into autumn or winter.

  4. 4

    Trace

    Trace the big word AUTUMN and write it on your own.

  5. 5

    Check

    Point at each column and name what makes it that season.

Before you start, have the words ready: What autumn looks like (falling leaves, wind) versus winter (snow, bare trees), and which clothes belong to each.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

The two cold seasons look and feel different — and they ask for different clothes.

Sorting two similar-but-different groups sharpens comparison — the skill underneath all later classification.

  • Comparing two seasons
  • Clothing vocabulary
  • Cutting and sorting
  • Fine motor control
  • Word tracing
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: Two chilly seasons, two different looks. Let us sort out which is which.

Questions to ask: What do you wear in autumn that you still wear in winter? What changes first?

Parent tips: Keep the cut pieces in a small bowl so none wander off mid-session.

Home practice: On a cool morning, decide together which season it feels like before you dress.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 34 · AGES 4–5

Autumn Weather and Clothes Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A autumn weather and clothes worksheet for ages 4–5: match the windy-day words, circle cool-day clothes, sort autumn from winter and trace the word AUTUMN. Printable.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/autumn-weather-and-clothes/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Match

    Draw a line from each autumn weather picture to its word.

  2. 2

    Circle

    Circle the clothes for a cool autumn day.

  3. 3

    Sort

    Put each picture in the autumn or the winter column.

  4. 4

    Trace

    Trace the word AUTUMN, then write it in the box.

  5. 5

    Say

    Name your own autumn outfit out loud when the sheet is done.

Before you start, have the words ready: The words wind, leaf, cloud and beanie, and the feeling of a cool day versus a cold one.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

Autumn has its own weather — wind, falling leaves, grey clouds — and its own clothes.

Dressing for the weather is a daily decision; this sheet makes the autumn version of it explicit and practised.

  • Autumn weather words
  • Dressing decisions
  • Sorting
  • Tracing and writing
  • Observation
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: Autumn is the wind-and-leaves season. What does it ask us to wear?

Questions to ask: Is today an autumn day or a winter day? How did you know?

Parent tips: Follow the sheet with the real thing: check the day together at the door tomorrow morning.

Home practice: Build the actual autumn outfit together — each piece named as it goes on.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 34 · AGES 4–5

Cloud Types Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A cloud types worksheet for ages 4–5: match cumulus, stratus and cirrus to their names, circle the fluffy cloud, sort fluffy from flat and trace the word CLOUD. Printable.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/cloud-types/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Match

    Draw a line from each cloud picture to its name.

  2. 2

    Circle

    Circle the cloud that looks fluffy.

  3. 3

    Sort

    Cut and paste each cloud into fluffy or flat.

  4. 4

    Trace

    Trace the big dotted word CLOUD and write it too.

  5. 5

    Look

    Match the sheet to a real cloud out of the window.

Before you start, have the words ready: The three cloud names on the sheet (cumulus, stratus, cirrus) and the fluffy-versus-flat contrast.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

Clouds come in kinds — fluffy piles, flat layers, wispy streaks — and each has a name.

Naming kinds of one thing — clouds — is classification practice with a daily show overhead.

  • Cloud names
  • Observation and comparison
  • Sorting into groups
  • Word tracing
  • Sky vocabulary
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: Clouds are not all the same — some sit in piles, some lie flat. Let us learn their names.

Questions to ask: Which cloud is out today? Does it look like the fluffy pile or the flat layers?

Parent tips: Keep the sheet on the window ledge for a week and re-check the real sky with it.

Home practice: Watch the sky at breakfast tomorrow and name every cloud you both see.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 34 · AGES 4–5

Cloudy Weather Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A cloudy weather worksheet for ages 4–5: circle the cloudy skies, match weather to picture, pick the right clothes, complete the pattern and trace the word CLOUDY. Printable.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/cloudy-weather/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Circle

    Circle every cloudy-sky picture in the grid.

  2. 2

    Match

    Match each weather picture to its word.

  3. 3

    Choose

    Circle the clothes that suit a cloudy day.

  4. 4

    Trace

    Trace the big word CLOUDY and write it on your own.

  5. 5

    Draw

    Finish the pattern boxes, then draw the cloudy sky scene.

Before you start, have the words ready: What a cloudy sky looks like next to sunny, rainy and snowy ones, and which clothes fit a grey day.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

A grey sky is weather too — cloudy has a name, a look and its own clothes.

Grey days confuse small children most; naming cloudy gives the day a handle and kills the gloom.

  • Weather recognition
  • Clothing choices
  • Pattern completion
  • Tracing and writing
  • Careful looking
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: The sun is hiding today — that has a name too. Let us find the cloudy pictures.

Questions to ask: What does the sky look like right now? What should we wear for it?

Parent tips: Take the sheet to a window; real sky beats remembered sky at this age.

Home practice: Make tomorrow a forecast: tonight your child predicts sunny or cloudy, and morning checks it.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 34 · AGES 4–5

Daylight: Sunrise and Sunset Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A daylight worksheet for ages 4–5: match sunrise, noon, sunset and night, compare which day has more daylight and trace the word DAYLIGHT. Printable.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/daylight-sunrise-sunset/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Match

    Draw a line from each sun position to its time of day.

  2. 2

    Compare

    Circle the day with the most daylight.

  3. 3

    Order

    Put the sun-arc pictures in order from morning to night.

  4. 4

    Trace

    Trace the big word DAYLIGHT and write it too.

  5. 5

    Draw

    Draw your own sunset in the last box.

Before you start, have the words ready: Sunrise, noon, sunset and night as positions of the sun — and that summer days are longer.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

The sun makes the day; where it sits in the sky tells you the time.

Ordering the day by the sun builds time sense before clocks — the oldest clock there is.

  • Time-of-day vocabulary
  • Sun position and shadow sense
  • Comparing lengths
  • Tracing and writing
  • Drawing what you see
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: The sun walks across the sky every day. Let us learn its road.

Questions to ask: Where is the sun when we eat breakfast? Where is it at bedtime in summer?

Parent tips: This sheet pairs with the rainy-day one — short daylight and long daylight in one week.

Home practice: Catch a real sunset once this week and name what you see with the sheet words.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 34 · AGES 4–5

Four Seasons Matching Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A four seasons matching worksheet for ages 4–5: match spring, summer, autumn and winter to their pictures, circle the snowiest season, sort the clothes and trace the word WINTER. Printable.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/four-seasons-matching/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Match

    Draw a line from each season name to its picture.

  2. 2

    Circle

    Circle the season with the most snow.

  3. 3

    Sort

    Cut and paste the clothes into winter or summer.

  4. 4

    Trace

    Trace the big word WINTER, then write it yourself.

  5. 5

    Draw

    Finish the flower-sun-leaf-snow pattern, then draw a winter scene.

Before you start, have the words ready: The four season names and one clear picture clue for each — blossom, beach, falling leaves, snow.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

The year comes in four seasons, each with its own look, weather and clothes.

The season cycle is the first big pattern a child meets that repeats every year — naming it orders the whole world.

  • Season names and order
  • Matching pictures to words
  • Clothing sorts
  • Pattern completion
  • Word tracing
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: A year has four seasons and each one changes the world outside. Let us match them up.

Questions to ask: Which season is it right now? What will come after it?

Parent tips: Sing the four season names in order before starting; the sheet then checks itself.

Home practice: Start a season wall at home — one drawing per season, added when each arrives.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 34 · AGES 4–5

Ice, Frost and Melting Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A ice and melting worksheet for ages 4–5: circle the frost, match frozen to melted, order the melting steps, find what melts ice fastest and trace the word ICE. Printable.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/ice-frost-melting/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Circle

    Circle the picture that shows frost.

  2. 2

    Match

    Match each frozen thing to its melted version.

  3. 3

    Order

    Put the melting ice pictures in order from start to puddle.

  4. 4

    Trace

    Trace the big word ICE and write it on your own.

  5. 5

    Draw

    Draw what the melted ice shape looks like at the end.

Before you start, have the words ready: The words frost, melt and puddle, and the idea that warmth (sun, hands, warm air) does the melting.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

Ice is water gone cold, and warmth turns it back — melting has an order and a cause.

Reversible change — freeze it, melt it — is a first science law children can watch in a glass of water.

  • State-of-matter words
  • Ordering a process
  • Predicting outcomes
  • Tracing and writing
  • Observation
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: Ice is just water wearing its winter coat. Warmth takes the coat back off.

Questions to ask: What made the ice disappear? Where does the puddle come from?

Parent tips: Freeze a small toy in a cube before the session — the sheet predicts, the cube proves.

Home practice: Leave two ice cubes out — one sunny window, one dark shelf — and race them.

Light Sources Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A light sources worksheet for ages 4–5: sort the light makers from the dark things, circle, match and trace the word LIGHT. Printable for ages 4–5.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/light-sources/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Sort

    Put each picture into gives light or does not.

  2. 2

    Circle

    Circle every picture that makes its own light.

  3. 3

    Match

    Trace

Parent tips: Do this one at dusk with the room lamp as the demo.

Home practice: Tonight, list every light you both see on the way to bed — real light-source spotting.

Order of Seasons: Tree Changes Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A seasons-and-trees worksheet for ages 4–5: order the same tree through spring, summer, autumn and winter, match leaf colours and trace the word SEASON. Printable.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/order-of-seasons-tree-changes/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

Questions to ask: Which tree is outside your window right now? What comes next for it?

Precipitation: Hail, Sleet and Snow Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A precipitation worksheet for ages 4–5: name what falls from storm clouds, sort frozen from liquid, count snowflakes and trace the word HAIL. Printable for ages 4–5.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/precipitation-hail-sleet-snow/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Name

  2. 2

    Sort

    Sort the pictures into ice or water.

  3. 3

    Count

    Count the snowflakes and write the number.

  4. 4

  • Sorting by state
  • Counting

  • Careful looking

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Mark

    Read each sky picture and mark it safe or unsafe for kite flying.

  2. 2

    Circle

    Circle the item that protects you from strong sun.

  3. 3

    Match

    Draw a line from lightning, thunder and rainbow to their pictures.

  4. 4

    Trace

    Trace the big word RAINBOW and write it on your own.

  5. 5

    Draw

    Draw your rainbow-after-rain in the last box.

Before you start, have the words ready: The words safe and unsafe, lightning, thunder, rainbow — and hat-sunglasses shade as sun protection.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

Weather decides what is safe: kites want calm skies, storms want us inside, sun wants hats.

Safety rules stick when a child sorts them on paper first — the sheet does the rehearsing before real wind does.

  • Safety judgement
  • Weather words
  • Matching
  • Tracing and writing
  • Decision making
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: Kites love some skies and hate others. Let us learn which is which.

Questions to ask: What do we do when thunder starts? Where is the safest place you know?

Parent tips: Pair the sheet with a real kite on a calm day — the words go live immediately.

Home practice: Name the sun-protection trio — hat, glasses, shade — before the next sunny outing.

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/weather-chart-bar-graph/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Read

    Read the weather chart for the week, one day at a time.

  2. 2

    Count

    Count the sunny days and write the number in the box.

  3. 3

    Compare

    Circle more or fewer for the rainy and the cloudy days.

  4. 4

    Colour

    Colour the bar graph to show how many days each weather had.

  5. 5

    Trace

    Trace the words WEATHER CHART and write them below.

Before you start, have the words ready: How to read the chart one day at a time, and that a bar's height shows how many.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

A week of weather can be counted, compared and drawn as bars — data hiding in plain sky.

This is a first graph built from real weather, which makes numbers about something a child can point at out of the window.

  • Reading a chart
  • Counting to three
  • Comparing more and fewer
  • Bar graphs
  • Word tracing
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: Seven days, one chart — let us count what the sky did all week.

Questions to ask: Which weather won the week? Which day would you pick for a picnic?

Parent tips: Keep the finished graph on the fridge and start a fresh one next Sunday.

Home practice: Start a real week-chart on the fridge tonight: one sticker or scribble a day.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 34 · AGES 4–5

Weather and Seasons Chart Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A weather and seasons worksheet for ages 4–5: answer the chart questions, match sunny, cloudy and rainy, pick the right seasons, circle the spring things and draw today's weather. Printable.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/weather-chart-read-and-match/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Answer

    Look at the chart and circle the answer to both questions.

  2. 2

    Match

    Draw a line from each weather word to its picture.

  3. 3

    Choose

    Circle the right season for the snow scene and the beach.

  4. 4

    Circle

    Circle everything that belongs in spring.

  5. 5

    Draw

    Draw today's weather in the box, then check it against the window.

Before you start, have the words ready: Sunny, cloudy and rainy as chart words, plus the season a snowy scene and a beach scene belong to.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

Weather words answer questions, and seasons pick their own pictures — reading the sky is a two-part skill.

Answering a question from a chart is early reading and early science holding hands.

  • Chart reading
  • Season choosing
  • Sorting by season
  • Word tracing
  • Weather drawing
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: This chart asks two questions — read it like a detective and circle what you know.

Questions to ask: Which season is our beach picture? Have we ever seen snow like the first one?

Parent tips: Swap seats afterwards and let your child interview you with the two chart questions.

Home practice: On the next car ride, spot one thing from the spring row out of the window.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 34 · AGES 4–5

Weather Forecast Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A weather forecast worksheet for ages 4–5: read three forecasts, circle the clear-sky one, match clear, foggy and stormy, choose what to take outside in fog and trace the word FORECAST. Printable.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/weather-forecast/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Read

    Read the three forecasts and circle the one that promises a clear sky.

  2. 2

    Match

    Draw a line from clear, foggy and stormy to their pictures.

  3. 3

    Trace

    Trace the word FORECAST and write it below.

  4. 4

    Circle

    Circle what you would take outside during fog.

  5. 5

    Draw

    Draw tomorrow's forecast symbol in the box, then check it in the morning.

Before you start, have the words ready: Clear, foggy and stormy as forecast words, and what each one looks like.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

A forecast is tomorrow's weather told in advance — reading it means you get a say in what to wear.

Forecasts turn weather from a surprise into a plan — a small but real feeling of being in charge.

  • Forecast words
  • Reading for meaning
  • Packing decisions
  • Word tracing
  • Predicting
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: Weather readers know tomorrow before it happens — let us read like they do.

Questions to ask: What would you pack for a foggy walk? What would you leave at home?

Parent tips: Read tomorrow's real forecast together tonight and let your child call it.

Home practice: Morning check: was your child's forecast symbol right? Let them announce it at breakfast.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 34 · AGES 4–5

Weather Map Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A weather map worksheet for ages 4–5: read the map of Northville, Rainville, Snowtown and Windyville, match the symbols, circle the coldest town and trace the word MAP. Printable.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/weather-map/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Read

    Look at the map and say each town's weather out loud.

  2. 2

    Match

    Draw a line from each symbol to the right town on the blank map.

  3. 3

    Circle

    Circle the town with the coldest weather.

  4. 4

    Trace

    Trace the word MAP, then write it on your own.

  5. 5

    Point

    Point at the map and name the town you would visit — and say why.

Before you start, have the words ready: The four map symbols — sun, rain, snow and wind — and the four town names they match.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

Different places can have different weather at the very same moment — a map shows it all at once.

Reading a map spreads thinking across space instead of one page — geography starts exactly here.

  • Map reading
  • Symbol matching
  • Comparing places
  • Word tracing
  • Cold-weather reasoning
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: Four towns, one island, four different skies — let us read them all at once.

Questions to ask: Which town is ours on this map? What would you pack for Snowtown?

Parent tips: Draw your own family onto the map — which town would your house be?

Home practice: Open a real weather map on a phone together and find your own town on it.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 34 · AGES 4–5

Weather Safety Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A weather safety worksheet for ages 4–5: decide safe or unsafe, circle where to go in a thunderstorm, match stay dry, stay warm and drink water, and trace the word SAFETY. Printable, age-honest, no scare tactics.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/weather-safety/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Mark

    Mark each picture SAFE or UNSAFE — trust your first answer.

  2. 2

    Circle

    Circle where a family should go when thunder starts.

  3. 3

    Match

    Draw a line from each rule to the picture that shows it.

  4. 4

    Trace

    Trace the word SAFETY and write it in the box.

  5. 5

    Draw

    Draw one way to stay safe in hot weather.

Before you start, have the words ready: The four scenes, the thunder shelter answer, and the three rules: stay dry, stay warm, drink water.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

Weather has rules that keep us comfortable and safe — dry in rain, warm in cold, water in heat, indoors in a storm.

Practising safety choices on paper makes the real ones come out automatically — rehearsal without risk.

  • Safety decisions
  • Storm routine
  • Rule matching
  • Word tracing
  • Drawing safety
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: Weather is strong, and we are smart — let us learn the moves for every kind of day.

Questions to ask: Where do we go when thunder rumbles? What do we drink on a hot day?

Parent tips: Walk the real storm plan once after the sheet: which room, which seat, which toy.

Home practice: Pack a small weather bag together — hat for sun, umbrella for rain — and keep it by the door.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 34 · AGES 4–5

Weather Tools Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A weather tools worksheet for ages 4–5: match each tool to its use, circle the temperature tool, count the windsock stripes, sort the tools and trace the words WEATHER TOOL. Printable.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/weather-tools/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Match

    Draw a line from each tool to the job it does.

  2. 2

    Circle

    Circle the tool that measures temperature.

  3. 3

    Count

    Count the stripes on each windsock and write the numbers.

  4. 4

    Sort

    Put each tool into measures rain or measures wind.

  5. 5

    Design

    Design your own weather tool in the box and name it.

Before you start, have the words ready: The four tools by name, and the one job that belongs to each.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

Weather is measured with real tools — a thermometer for heat, a gauge for rain, a windsock and weathervane for wind.

Tools turn watching weather into measuring it — the moment science stops being looking and starts being knowing.

  • Tool names
  • Matching jobs
  • Counting stripes
  • Sorting by purpose
  • Inventing and drawing
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: Scientists never guess the weather — they ask their tools. Meet the four of them.

Questions to ask: Which tool would you want on the balcony? What does our thermometer at home say?

Parent tips: A pinwheel or cheap windsock on the balcony makes this sheet come alive all week.

Home practice: Build the box invention for real from a cup and a straw, if the design bug bites.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 34 · AGES 4–5

Weather Words Matching Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A weather words worksheet for ages 4–5: match sunny, rainy, cloudy and windy, circle the rainy-day clothes, sort hot things from cold things and trace the word SUNNY. Printable.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/weather-words-matching/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Match

    Draw a line from each weather word to its picture.

  2. 2

    Circle

    Circle the clothes a rainy day really needs.

  3. 3

    Trace

    Trace the word SUNNY and write it on the line.

  4. 4

    Sort

    Put each picture into hot or cold.

  5. 5

    Draw

    Draw the weather outside your window right now.

Before you start, have the words ready: Sunny, rainy, cloudy and windy by picture, and which clothes answer a rainy day.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

Every kind of sky has a word, and every word asks for its own clothes and things.

Word-and-picture matching is the strongest vocabulary glue there is — weather words are just the friendly subject.

  • Weather vocabulary
  • Clothing choices
  • Hot and cold sorting
  • Word tracing
  • Drawing the day
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: Four skies, four words — let us wire them together so they never come apart.

Questions to ask: What word is our sky today? What would you wear for it?

Parent tips: Do the draw box standing at a real window — checking beats remembering.

Home practice: Tonight at dinner, name today's weather word and one thing you wore because of it.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 34 · AGES 4–5

Wind Direction and Compass Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A wind direction worksheet for ages 4–5: write left, right, up and down for the arrows, match the compass directions, circle the flag blowing left and trace the word WIND. Printable.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/wind-direction-compass/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Follow

    Follow each arrow and write the direction it shows.

  2. 2

    Match

    Draw a line from each compass word to the compass rose.

  3. 3

    Circle

    Circle the flag that is blowing to the left.

  4. 4

    Trace

    Trace the word WIND and write it on your own.

  5. 5

    Face

    Stand and face north together, then spin to south for a giggle.

Before you start, have the words ready: The four arrow words and the four compass points on the rose.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

Wind has a direction, and direction has words — left, right, up and down first, then north, south, east and west.

Direction words do double duty — they read the wind today and maps tomorrow.

  • Direction words
  • Compass points
  • Observing flags
  • Word tracing
  • Left and right certainty
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: Wind never sits still — but it always goes somewhere. Let us name where.

Questions to ask: Which way is the washing-line flag pointing? Where does north sit in our bedroom?

Parent tips: A phone compass turns the bedside into a treasure hunt: find north, then east.

Home practice: Watch a real flag or treetop on the walk home and call the direction together.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 34 · AGES 4–5

Windy Weather Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A windy weather worksheet for ages 4–5: match sunny, cloudy, rainy and windy, circle the windy-day things, complete the weather pattern and trace the word WINDY. Printable.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/weather-seasons-and-what-we-wear/worksheets/windy-weather/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Match

    Draw a line from each weather word to its picture.

  2. 2

    Circle

    Circle the things you use on a windy day.

  3. 3

    Trace

    Trace the word WINDY and write it below.

  4. 4

    Pattern

    Finish the sky pattern in the last box.

  5. 5

    Draw

    Draw your own windy day — hair flying, leaves going.

Before you start, have the words ready: Windy next to its three cousins sunny, rainy and cloudy, and the kite as the windy-day star.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

Windy is the weather you can hear — and it brings its own things: kites up, hats held, umbrellas tucked.

A sky pattern that repeats teaches prediction: what comes next is thinking, not guessing.

  • Weather vocabulary
  • Windy-day choices
  • Pattern completion
  • Word tracing
  • Drawing movement
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: You cannot see wind — only what it pushes. Let us spot the pushing day.

Questions to ask: What does wind do to your hair? What flies in wind that will not fly on a still day?

Parent tips: Throw a paper aeroplane on a still day and a windy one, then report back to the sheet.

Home practice: On the next windy walk, name three things the wind is moving — bins, leaves, anything.
